thread:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert — elevated errors and timeouts for /v1/generate in us-west-2. p99=18.3s, p95=2.1s, error rate ~18% over last 2m. Alert started 2026-03-15T15:04:22Z

monitoring-bot: alert details -> https://monitoring.redwood.example/alerts/1833214422 :link:

dana_oncall: i'm oncall, ack. paging infra/runtime. any deploys in the last 10m?

deploy-bot: CI deploy completed: service=api-runtime namespace=prod rollouts/api-runtime v13->v14 completed at 2026-03-15T15:02:10Z by pipeline/main #deploy-7421

carol_platform: confirmed — canary promoted at 15:02. nothing else.

ben_runtime: i'm jumping in. grabbing traces and request logs. initial look: tail of requests show an uptick in connection errors and `context deadline exceeded` at ~15:02:30. looks like runtime backend calls to kv-cache are stalling.

ben_runtime: snippets from logs:
```
[15:02:31] rpc: dial tcp 10.45.23.7:11211: i/o timeout
[15:02:32] request_id=abc123 error="context deadline exceeded" route="/v1/generate"
[15:02:33] worker: queue_wait>2000ms inflight=260 max_inflight=250
```

dana_oncall: looks like connection pool saturation. what's inflight at peak?

ben_runtime: p95 inflight window jumped to ~240-270 for the runtime pod group. config max_inflight_requests is 250 for that pool. we're hitting the cap which yields queuing -> timeouts.

frank_ic: assigning incident commander to consolidate. frank_ic taking IC. frank_ic here — quick hypothesis: new runtime change in v14 changed connection handling or introduced a blocking call to cache warming. Need to decide rollback vs mitigation.

eve_support: CS reports ~120 customers saw failures in the last 10m. some enterprise customers had timed-out requests in dashboards. collecting customer ids now.

ben_runtime: i can try to drop `max_inflight_requests` to limit queuing? that won't help existing inflight. safer immediate action is rollback to v13 to restore known-good behaviour.

carol_platform: rollback path is available. kubectl rollback or `kubectl rollout undo` works; we have traffic shift scripts too.

dana_oncall: what's risk of rollback? any db migrations?

carol_platform: no migrations in that deploy. canary had 10k requests during verification and looked fine, but global load differs. rollback should be low risk.

frank_ic: decision: immediate rollback to v13. frank_ic -> dana_oncall coordinate with platform for rollback. ben_runtime continue to monitor during rollback. ops-bot please pause autoscaler policies briefly to avoid oscillation.

ops-bot: Autoscaling policy actions paused for service=api-runtime for 10 minutes.

carol_platform: executing rollback now. command:
```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/api-runtime --to-revision=13
```

deploy-bot: rollback job started by carol_platform at 2026-03-15T15:10:12Z. rollout status streaming...

deploy-bot: rollout complete. deployment/api-runtime now at revision=13 (v13).

dana_oncall: can everyone confirm metrics and error rate?

monitoring-bot: post-rollback metrics (15:12—15:16): error rate down to 2.3%, p99=420ms, p95=210ms.

ben_runtime: i'm seeing error rate drop on runtime pods. connection errors cleared. KV cache latency back to normal. looks good from runtime side.

eve_support: CS: customer-impact reduced. enterprise incident count down to ~4 active reports — proactively reaching out.

frank_ic: good. frank_ic assigning follow-ups:
- ben_runtime to collect diagnostic traces and config diff between v13/v14 (why pool exceeded).
- carol_platform to hold v14 and block re-promote until root cause found.
- dana_oncall to run post-rollback checks for the next hour and hand off to next oncall.
- eve_support to prepare customer comms draft.

ben_runtime: noted. quick diff snapshot:
```diff
- connection_pool.size = 250
+ connection_pool.size = 250
+ warm_on_start = true          # v14 added synchronous warm path to kv cache
+ cache_warm_timeout = 5s      # new blocking call introduced during startup/first requests
```

ben_runtime: early theory: v14 added a synchronous cache warm path that sometimes blocks on backend memcached during high load, resulting in inflight buildups.

carol_platform: v14 is marked hold in rollout controller and promotion disabled.

frank_ic: timeline & notes captured. frank_ic creating incident ticket and will join postmortem. :white_check_mark:

monitoring-bot: incident record created: https://incidents.redwood.example/incident/IR-2026-0315-1833214422

dana_oncall: i'm going to run a quick smoke test suite across regions and then handoff in 30m. if anything degrades, re-alert here.

eve_support: customer message draft: "We've identified a recent deploy caused elevated timeouts for some requests. We rolled back the change and systems are responding normally. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with details." Sending to legal/commms for sign-off.

frank_ic: handoff plan: dana_oncall -> next_oncall (ben_runtime) at 15:45 UTC. frank_ic will coordinate postmortem. Add logs, rollout artifacts, and the v14 artifact to the incident ticket.

dana_oncall: handing off in 30m. monitoring alerts will remain active. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: note: v14 artifact id=sha256:deadbeef preserved in registry, tag=staging/v14.

ben_runtime: collecting flamegraphs and request traces. suspects: synchronous cache warm and memcached connection wobble. will push a safe fix branch that toggles warm_on_start off and add a timeout guard.

frank_ic: closing shift in channel — ongoing work in incident ticket. if customer-impacting regressions show up, re-open channel with `SEV2` prefix.

monitoring-bot: all good for now. continuing to watch. :eyes:

-- end of thread --
